semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: The term 'interpretability' without any specifications or distinctions can include model-agnostic approaches, as it generally refers to the ability to understand and interpret the decisions of models regardless of their architecture.

parent_domains.justification: 'Interpretability' is a broader category encompassing all forms of interpretability research including model-agnostic methods.
As 'model-agnostic interpretability' falls under the general umbrella of interpreting models, 'model interpretability' serves as a broader category.
This domain includes both interpretability and explainability, covering various aspects including model-agnostic approaches, serving as a broader category.

closest_parent_domain.justification: 'Model interpretability' directly aligns with 'model-agnostic interpretability,' since the focus is on understanding models irrespective of their specifics, making it the nearest broader category.

child_domains.justification: A specific form of interpretability focusing on neural networks, which falls under the broader category of model-agnostic interpretability methods.
A specialized form of interpretability dealing with language models, which is a subset of model-agnostic interpretability as it pertains to specific models.

closest_child_domain.justification: Neural network interpretability focuses on a common and significant type of model, making it more directly beneath the umbrella of model-agnostic approaches.

sibling_domains.justification: Instead of model-agnostic, focuses on making specific models inherently interpretable, sharing the broad domain of interpretability with semantic equivalence in focus.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: While not agnostic, interpretable machine learning involves broader techniques to make the learning process interpretable and hence has the closest operational focus to model-agnostic approaches.
